system.name: TAPAS
system.one_liner: a thermal- and power-aware framework for cloud LLM inference clusters that places VMs, routes requests, and reconfigures instances

components.name: Profiles
components.role: repository of historical/live telemetry (temperature, power, airflow, DC layout, load) TAPAS maintains and uses for decision-making

components.name: LLM Temp/Power
components.role: profile metric tracking LLM inference temperature/power behavior

components.name: DC layout
components.role: profile metric describing the datacenter's physical layout

components.name: SaaS/IaaS Operator
components.role: actor who triggers IaaS/SaaS VM creations

components.name: VM Allocator
components.role: extends the existing per-cluster VM Allocator; places new GPU workload VMs within cooling/power constraints using Profiles

components.name: SaaS Frontends
components.role: group of per-endpoint frontends serving SaaS requests

components.name: Endpoint A
components.role: one SaaS endpoint among several stacked endpoints

components.name: Load Balancer
components.role: extends the existing per-endpoint Load Balancer; routes LLM inference requests across SaaS VM instances

components.name: Aisle 1
components.role: physical datacenter aisle containing rows of racks/instances

components.name: SaaS-B
components.role: a SaaS VM instance (tagged IC, has an Instance Configurator)

components.name: SaaS-A
components.role: a SaaS VM instance, deployed as multiple instances each paired with an Instance Configurator

components.name: Instance Configurator
components.role: TAPAS's new per-SaaS VM Instance Configurator that reconfigures SaaS VMs to manage load spikes and emergencies

components.name: SaaS-C
components.role: a SaaS VM instance (tagged IC, has an Instance Configurator)

content.key_idea: TAPAS extends a cloud LLM inference cluster's VM Allocator and Load Balancer, adds a per-SaaS Instance Configurator, and maintains a Profiles store of thermal/power/airflow telemetry to jointly drive VM placement, request routing, and instance reconfiguration.
content.reading_order: top band of Profiles metrics first, then the operator/user actors, VM Allocator, and SaaS Frontends' Load Balancer, into Aisle 1's rows of SaaS/IaaS instances

style.stroke: thin black strokes; dashed borders group logical regions (Aisle 1, Rows, SaaS Frontends); dotted gray lines carry profile data; solid red lines/boxes highlight the request-routing path
style.font: Calibri sans, bold for major labels
style.arrows: dotted gray arrows for profile data feeding decisions, dashed black arrows for VM placement/creation, solid red arrows for LLM-inference request routing
style.icons: vector icons for the person actors (operator/user), server rack/DC layout, VM boxes, and database-cylinder icons on Profiles/VM Allocator/Instance Configurator

encoding.color_means: gold = Profiles data store and VM Allocator, tan = IaaS instances, light green = SaaS instances, dark green = the new Instance Configurator, pale blue = Load Balancer/SaaS Frontends, red = the live LLM-inference request-routing path
encoding.line_style_means: dotted lines = profile data feeding decisions, dashed lines = VM placement/creation actions, solid red lines = live inference request routing
encoding.emphasis: red highlight boxes single out the two 'SaaS-A' Instance Configurator instances and the routing path between them, spotlighting TAPAS's new per-SaaS reconfiguration capability
reusable_patterns: central telemetry/profile store feeding multiple downstream control components via dotted arrows
physical datacenter layout (aisle/row/instance) nested inside a logical architecture diagram
weaknesses: extremely dense (600 shapes, 72 text boxes) with many small repeated instance boxes (SaaS/IaaS-N) that require careful visual tracing

evidence: TAPAS (1) extends existing components of conventional cloud LLM inference clusters (e.g., per-cluster VM Allocator
(2) introduces a per-SaaS VM Instance Configurator, and (3) maintains multiple Profiles.
TAPAS focuses on three core aspects: VM placement, LLM inference request routing, and instance configuration.

summary: Figure 17 is TAPAS's architecture overview. A top orange band of Profiles (LLM Temp/Power, DC layout, T_GPU/T_inlet/T_outside, Load_DC/Load_GPU, Power_GPU/Server/Row, Airflow_Aisle/Serv) feeds decision-making, via dotted arrows, into the VM Allocator, SaaS Frontends, and the datacenter's Aisle 1 rows, while offline profiling flows back up from the aisle. An SaaS/IaaS Operator triggers VM creations at the VM Allocator, which places VMs (dashed arrows) into Row 1 and Row 2 racks of SaaS and IaaS instances. An SaaS User's LLM Inference request enters the Load Balancer inside Endpoint A; a red-highlighted path then routes SaaS-A requests among multiple SaaS-A instances, each paired with TAPAS's new Instance Configurator, which reconfigures SaaS VMs to handle load spikes and emergencies. Gold marks Profiles/VM Allocator, tan marks IaaS instances, green marks SaaS instances and Instance Configurators, and red marks the live request-routing path.
